_comment: One remediation, twenty-eight days, seven deliveries. Business dates are weeks apart and are what every figure is computed from; wall-clock is compressed when this is replayed. Every event falls on a business day. Nothing here is a transition -- each event names a destination and the lifecycle decides whether the case may go there. `error_bps` sits deliberately between the isolated (50) and recurring (20) materiality thresholds, so the outcome depends on the prior errors below and on nothing else. One event is deliberately out of order: a payment release arriving before approval. The lifecycle has no edge from awaiting_approval to compensation_in_flight, so it is refused, the denial is recorded, and the case does not move.

events.note: published NAV for 2026-08-17 misstated by 30bps: stale USD rate applied to the ADR sleeve
transfer agency reports who dealt at the misstated price
materiality assessed against the fund's recent error history
compensation plan drafted; requires four eyes
payment file released early by the settlement system, before approval was recorded
approved by two signatories outside the fleet
payments instructed for the affected holders
every affected investor's compensation confirmed, 29 days after the valuation point

prior_errors.note: pricing error on the ADR sleeve, 62bps, compensated
stale FX rate applied to the EUR share class, 88bps, compensated
corporate action booked a day late, 54bps, compensated
